senses.en: happening by chance or unexpectedly or unintentionally

examples.text: We check everything because an inadvertent error could be disastrous.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 inadvertēns에서 왔습니다. 마음을 그쪽으로 돌리지(advert) 않은 채 하는 행동이 '무심코 한'입니다.

senses.en: total lack of meaning or ideas

examples.text: The inanity of the talk show's banter left viewers wondering why they had bothered to tune in at all.

senses.en: Something that is inane.

examples.text: Working in any bureaucracy means being bedeviled by inanities daily.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inānitās '텅 빈 상태'에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 속이 텅 비어 '무의미함'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: without or deprived of the use of speech or words
senses.ko: 말을 못 하는, 분명하게 표현하지 못하는

examples.text: Overwhelmed by grief, the witness became inarticulate and could only shake his head when questioned.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inarticulātus에서 왔습니다. 말을 마디마디 또렷이 나누지 못해 분명히 표현하지 못합니다.

senses.en: In like degree; in like manner; to the same or similar degree; likewise.

examples.text: The argument is persuasive inasmuch as it rests on evidence that independent researchers have repeatedly confirmed.

origin.ko: in, as, much가 하나로 합쳐진 말입니다. '그만큼의 정도로'라는 뜻에서 '~인 점에서'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Innate; possessed by an organism at birth.

examples.text: inborn talent

origin.ko: in(안)과 born(태어난)의 합성어입니다. 태어날 때부터 몸 안에 갖고 있다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: characterized by ardent emotion or intensity or brilliance

examples.text: The incandescent performance enraptured the audience.

senses.en: Emitting light as a result of being heated.

examples.text: The incandescent filament glowed steadily inside the glass bulb once the current reached it.

senses.en: Extremely angry; furious.

examples.text: She is incandescent with rage because someone stole her wallet.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incandescō '달아오르다'에서 왔고 candidus(하얀)가 뿌리입니다. 하얗게 달아올라 빛나는 모습입니다.

senses.en: make flesh-colored

examples.text: The setting sun seemed to incarnadine the clouds, turning the whole western sky a deep blood red.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 incarnadino '살빛'에서 왔고 라틴어 carō(살)가 뿌리입니다. 살빛에서 핏빛 붉은색으로 물들이는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: arousing to action or rebellion

examples.text: The senator's incendiary speech provoked angry protests outside the capitol within hours of its broadcast.

senses.en: involving deliberate burning of property

examples.text: Investigators concluded the warehouse blaze was caused by an incendiary device left near the loading dock.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incendiārius '불을 지르는'에서 왔고 incendō(불붙이다)가 뿌리입니다. 불을 붙이듯 사람들을 부추기는 선동적인 말이 되었습니다.

senses.en: make furious

examples.text: The company's decision to cut pensions without warning incensed employees across the country.

senses.en: a substance that produces a fragrant odor when burned

examples.text: The monks lit incense at dawn, and its sweet smoke drifted slowly through the stone hall.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incendō '불을 붙이다'에서 왔습니다. 마음에 불을 붙이듯 몹시 화나게 한다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: a positive motivational influence

examples.text: Tax credits give homeowners a strong incentive to install solar panels on their roofs.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 incentīvus '곡조를 시작하는'에서 왔습니다. 노래를 선창해 분위기를 띄우듯 행동을 북돋는 것입니다.

senses.en: uninterrupted in time and indefinitely long continuing

examples.text: The dog's incessant barking kept the girl awake all night.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 incessāns '멈추지 않는'에서 왔습니다. 멈추지 않고 이어지는 상태입니다.

senses.en: only partly in existence; imperfectly formed
senses.ko: 막 시작된, 아직 형태가 갖춰지지 않은

examples.text: The inchoate plan had no budget, no timeline, and only a vague sense of purpose.

senses.en: Chaotic, disordered, confused; also, incoherent, rambling.

examples.text: His inchoate ramblings left the committee unsure what exactly he was proposing.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incohātus '막 시작된, 미완성의'에서 왔고 incohō(시작하다)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: not of prime or central importance

examples.text: That character, though colorful, is incidental to the overall plot.

senses.en: occurring with or following as a consequence

examples.text: Injuries are incidental to contact sports: they're going to happen.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어에서 왔고 라틴어 incidere(우연히 떨어지다)가 뿌리입니다. 우연히 곁들여 일어난다는 데서 '부수적인'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: In an initial stage; beginning, starting, coming into existence.

examples.text: After 500 years, incipient towns appeared.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incipiēns '시작하는'에서 왔고 incipiō(시작하다)가 뿌리입니다. 막 손을 대기 시작한다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: having or demonstrating ability to recognize or draw fine distinctions

examples.text: The critic's incisive analysis exposed the flaw at the heart of the policy within a single paragraph.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 incīsīvus '자르는'에서 왔고 incīdō(안으로 베다)가 뿌리입니다. 칼처럼 깊이 베어 들어가는 날카로운 통찰입니다.

senses.en: (of weather or climate) severe

examples.text: The marathon was postponed because of inclement weather that made the course dangerously slick.

senses.en: used of persons or behavior; showing no clemency or mercy

examples.text: The inclement judge handed down the harshest sentence the law allowed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inclēmēns '인정사정없는, 거친'에서 왔습니다. clēmēns(온화한)에 부정 접두사가 붙어 궂은 날씨를 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: Having a tendency, preference, likelihood, or disposition.

examples.text: I am inclined to believe you.

senses.en: At an angle to the horizontal; slanted or sloped.

examples.text: The take-off ramp was inclined at 20 degrees.

origin.ko: incline(기울다)에서 온 말입니다. 마음이 어떤 쪽으로 기울어 있어 '~하는 경향이 있는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Including (almost) everything within its scope.

examples.text: An inclusive study of the region's history must consider the voices of its minority communities.

senses.en: Including the extremes as well as the area between.

examples.text: numbers 1 to 10 inclusive

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 inclūsīvus에서 왔고 라틴어 inclūsus(안에 닫힌)가 뿌리입니다. 모든 것을 울타리 안에 넣는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the quality of disagreeing; being unsuitable and inappropriate

examples.text: The incongruity of a marble fountain in the middle of the desert amused every passing tourist.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 incongruitās에서 왔습니다. 서로 함께 맞아떨어지지 않는 상태입니다.

senses.en: lacking in harmony or compatibility or appropriateness

examples.text: The glass tower looked incongruous beside the centuries-old stone cottages of the village.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incongruus에서 왔습니다. congruus(함께 맞는)에 부정 접두사가 붙어 어울리지 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lacking worth or importance

examples.text: The error was inconsequential and had no effect on the final results of the experiment.

senses.en: not following logically as a consequence
senses.ko: 논리적 귀결이 아닌, 앞뒤가 맞지 않는

examples.text: His conclusion was inconsequential, since it did not follow from any of the premises he had listed.

origin.ko: consequential(결과가 따르는, 중요한)에 부정 접두사가 붙은 말입니다. 따라오는 결과가 없을 만큼 하찮다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the quality of being changeable and variable

examples.text: The inconstancy of public opinion made it nearly impossible for pollsters to predict the election's outcome.

senses.en: unfaithfulness by virtue of being unreliable or treacherous

examples.text: His inconstancy in friendship left former allies unwilling to trust him again.

origin.ko: in-(않는)에 constancy(꾸준함)가 붙은 말입니다. 한자리에 굳게 서 있지 못하는 변덕을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: impossible to deny or disprove
senses.ko: 논란의 여지가 없는, 반박할 수 없는

examples.text: incontrovertible evidence

origin.ko: controvert(반박하다)에 부정 접두사가 붙은 말입니다. 반대쪽으로 돌려세울 수 없으니 반박할 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: make into a whole or make part of a whole

examples.text: She incorporated his suggestions into her proposal

senses.en: To form into a legal company.

examples.text: The company was incorporated in 1980.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 incorporō '몸으로 만들다'에서 왔습니다. 하나의 몸(corpus) 안으로 넣어 통합한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: impervious to correction by punishment

examples.text: The incorrigible prankster ignored every detention and kept scheming new tricks to play on his teachers.

senses.en: difficult or impossible to manage or control

examples.text: The committee found the backlog incorrigible, since no reorganization had ever managed to tame it.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incorrigibilis '고칠 수 없는'에서 왔습니다. corrigere(바로잡다)에 부정 접두사가 붙었습니다.

senses.en: not disposed or willing to believe; unbelieving

examples.text: The jury listened with incredulous expressions as the defendant described his improbable alibi.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incrēdulus '믿지 않는'에서 왔습니다. 믿지(cred) 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: teach and impress by frequent repetitions or admonitions

examples.text: inculcate values into the young generation

origin.ko: 라틴어 inculcō '밟아 넣다, 강요하다'에서 왔고 calx(발뒤꿈치)가 뿌리입니다. 발로 꾹꾹 밟아 다지듯 되풀이해 새겨 넣는다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: necessary (for someone) as a duty or responsibility; morally binding

examples.text: it is incumbent on them to pay their own debts

senses.en: currently holding an office

examples.text: the incumbent governor

senses.en: the official who holds an office

examples.text: The incumbent narrowly defeated her challenger after a bitter and expensive campaign.

origin.ko: 라틴어 incumbēns '기대고 누운'에서 왔고 incumbō(위에 얹히다)가 뿌리입니다. 어깨 위에 얹힌 책임이 '의무로 지워진'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: lacking propriety and good taste in manners and conduct

examples.text: The guest's indecorous remarks at the funeral shocked the grieving family.

origin.ko: 라틴어 indecōrus에서 왔습니다. decorous(품위 있는)에 부정 접두사가 붙었습니다.

senses.en: showing sustained enthusiastic action with unflagging vitality

examples.text: an indefatigable advocate of equal rights

origin.ko: 라틴어 indēfatīgābilis '지치지 않는'에서 왔습니다. 완전히 지칠 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: secure against future loss, damage, or liability; give security for

examples.text: The contract indemnifies the landlord against any claims arising from damage caused by tenants.

senses.en: To compensate or reimburse someone for some expense or injury.

examples.text: The insurer agreed to indemnify the family for the full cost of rebuilding their flooded home.

origin.ko: indemn(다치지 않은)에 -ify가 붙은 말입니다. 손해를 입지 않은 상태로 되돌려 놓는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: not precisely determined or established; not fixed or known in advance

examples.text: of indeterminate age

senses.en: of uncertain or ambiguous nature

examples.text: The painting's indeterminate shapes could be read as either clouds or waves, depending on the viewer.

origin.ko: determinate(경계가 정해진)에 부정 접두사가 붙은 말입니다. 경계(terminus)가 확정되지 않은 상태입니다.

senses.en: something that serves to indicate or suggest

examples.text: There's no indication that the fire was caused by criminals.

origin.ko: 라틴어 indicātiō에서 왔고 indicō(가리키다)가 뿌리입니다. 손가락으로 가리켜 보여 주는 것이 '징후'입니다.

senses.en: accuse formally of a crime

examples.text: his former manager was indicted for fraud

senses.en: To accuse of wrongdoing; charge.

examples.text: a book that indicts modern values

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 enditer '받아 적게 하다'에서 왔고 라틴어 dicere(말하다)가 뿌리입니다. 죄를 공식적으로 말해 선언하는 것이 '기소하다'입니다.

senses.en: an accusation of wrongdoing

examples.text: the book is an indictment of modern philosophy

senses.en: a formal document written for a prosecuting attorney charging a person with some offense

examples.text: The grand jury returned an indictment against the mayor on three counts of bribery.

origin.ko: 중세영어 endytement '고발 행위'에서 왔고 라틴어 dicere(말하다)가 뿌리입니다. 잘못을 공식적으로 말해 고발하는 일입니다.

senses.en: the trait of lacking enthusiasm for or interest in things generally

examples.text: Voter indifference was blamed for the record-low turnout in the local election.

senses.en: unbiased impartial unconcern

examples.text: The arbiter's indifference between the two parties reassured both sides that the ruling would be fair.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 indifferentia에서 왔습니다. 둘 사이에 차이를 두지 않아 어느 쪽에도 마음이 가지 않는 상태입니다.

senses.en: showing no care or concern in attitude or action

examples.text: indifferent to the sufferings of others

senses.en: fairly poor to not very good

examples.text: has an indifferent singing voice

origin.ko: 라틴어 indifferēns에서 왔습니다. 차이(different)를 두지 않아 어느 쪽에도 마음이 쏠리지 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a state of extreme poverty or destitution

examples.text: Having lost his business, he lived out his final years in indigence, relying on charity for meals.

origin.ko: 라틴어 indigentia에서 왔고 indigēre(필요로 하다)가 뿌리입니다. 필요한 것이 모자란 극심한 가난입니다.

senses.en: originating where it is found

examples.text: That style of pottery is indigenous to that region.

senses.en: Innate, inborn.

examples.text: Her indigenous talent for languages let her pick up new tongues with almost no formal study.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 indigenus '그 땅에서 태어난'에서 왔습니다. 안에서(indi) 태어난(gen) 토착의 존재입니다.

senses.en: poor enough to need help from others

examples.text: The clinic provides free care to indigent patients who cannot afford insurance.

origin.ko: 라틴어 indigēns '필요로 하는'에서 왔고 indigeō(부족하다)가 뿌리입니다. 필요한 것이 없는 가난한 상태입니다.

senses.en: angered at something unjust or wrong

examples.text: Indignant residents packed the town hall to protest the unfair closure of their school.

origin.ko: 라틴어 indignor '부당하다고 여기다'에서 왔고 dignus(합당한)가 뿌리입니다. 부당하다고 느끼니 분개하는 것입니다.

senses.en: failing to make or recognize distinctions

examples.text: The indiscriminate use of antibiotics has contributed to the rise of drug-resistant bacteria.

origin.ko: discriminate(구별하다)에 부정 접두사가 붙은 말입니다. 가려내지 않고 닥치는 대로 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: not to be dispensed with; essential

examples.text: foods indispensable to good nutrition

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 indispensābilis에서 왔습니다. 빼고 나눠 줄 수 없을 만큼 꼭 있어야 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: produce a literary work

examples.text: The poet retired to a cottage by the sea to indite a long elegy for her late mentor.

origin.ko: indict의 변형으로, 후기 라틴어 indictāre에서 왔습니다. 말한 것을 글로 받아 적는 데서 '쓰다, 짓다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: disinclined to work or exertion

examples.text: The indolent girl resisted doing her homework.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 indolēns '아프지 않은'에서 왔습니다. 고통을 느끼지 않으니 애써 일하지 않는 나태함이 되었습니다.

senses.en: characterized by hard work and perseverance

examples.text: He was a very industrious student at school.

origin.ko: 라틴어 industria '부지런함'에서 후기 라틴어 industriōsus와 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다.

senses.en: defying expression or description
senses.ko: 말로 표현할 수 없는, 형언할 수 없는

examples.text: Standing before the vast canyon at dawn, she felt an ineffable calm that no words could capture.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ineffābilis에서 왔습니다. 밖으로(ex) 말해 낼(fa) 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: impossible to avoid or evade

examples.text: Historians debate whether the empire's collapse was an ineluctable outcome of its economic decline.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inēlūctābilis에서 왔습니다. 몸부림쳐 빠져나올(ēluctor) 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: injustice by virtue of not conforming with rules or standards

examples.text: The report highlights the inequity in funding between wealthy and poor school districts.

origin.ko: in-(않는)에 equity(공평)가 붙은 말입니다. 공평하지 않은 상태입니다.

senses.en: slow and apathetic

examples.text: After the heavy meal, the guests lay inert on the sofas, too sleepy to continue the conversation.

senses.en: having only a limited ability to react chemically; chemically inactive

examples.text: Argon is an inert gas, so it is often used to protect metals during welding.

senses.en: unable to move or resist motion

examples.text: The inert body of the fallen tree blocked the narrow mountain road for two days.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 inerte를 거쳐 라틴어 iners '활동하지 않는'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: impervious to pleas, persuasion, requests, reason

examples.text: The inexorable negotiator ignored every plea for a compromise and held to his original terms.

senses.en: Impossible to prevent or stop; inevitable.

examples.text: The inexorable advance of the glacier eventually buried the village under a wall of ice.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inexōrābilis에서 왔고 ōs(입)가 뿌리입니다. 간청해서 마음을 움직일 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: incapable of failure or error

examples.text: No scientific method is infallible, which is why findings must be replicated by independent teams.

senses.en: Certain to produce the intended effect; sure.

examples.text: Try this infallible cure for hiccups.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 īnfallibilis에서 왔습니다. fallibilis(틀릴 수 있는)에 부정 접두사가 붙었습니다.

senses.en: not appropriate in application; defective

examples.text: an infelicitous remark

senses.en: marked by or producing unhappiness

examples.text: infelicitous circumstances

origin.ko: felicitous(알맞은)에 부정 접두사가 붙은 말입니다. 라틴어 fēlix(행복한)가 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: invade in great numbers

examples.text: the roaches infested our kitchen

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnfestus '적대적인'에서 고대 프랑스어 infester를 거쳐 왔습니다. 해로운 것이 떼로 들이닥쳐 괴롭힌다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: easily ignited

examples.text: Workers were warned to keep inflammable solvents away from the heaters in the storage room.

senses.en: Easily excited; set off by the slightest excuse; easily enraged or inflamed.

examples.text: With tempers already inflammable after the long strike, a single insult was enough to spark a brawl.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnflammāre '불을 붙이다'에서 왔습니다. 불꽃(flamma)이 붙을 수 있다는 뜻으로, in-은 부정이 아니라 '안으로'입니다.

senses.en: arousing to action or rebellion

examples.text: Sam posted an inflammatory comment to the newsgroup.

senses.en: characterized or caused by inflammation

examples.text: Doctors prescribed a drug to reduce the inflammatory response in her damaged joints.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnflammātōrius에서 왔습니다. 마음에 불꽃을 일으켜 사람들을 격앙시킨다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: give character or essence to

examples.text: His sense of religion informs everything he writes.

senses.en: act as an informer

examples.text: She had informed on her own parents for years

senses.en: impart knowledge of some fact, state of affairs, or event to

examples.text: I informed him of his rights

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnfōrmō '형태를 만들다, 가르치다'에서 왔습니다. 안에 모양(form)을 새겨 특징을 부여한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: showing inventiveness and skill

examples.text: That is an ingenious model of the atom.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ingenium '타고난 재능'에서 왔습니다. 몸 안에 타고난 재능이 있다는 데서 '독창적인'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: an artless innocent young girl (especially as portrayed on the stage)
senses.ko: 순진한 젊은 여자, 순진한 아가씨 역

examples.text: The director cast her as the wide-eyed ingenue who is gradually drawn into the city's corrupt politics.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 ingénu(순진한)의 여성형이고, 라틴어 ingenuus에서 왔습니다. 무대의 순진한 아가씨 역을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: the power of creative imagination

examples.text: The pyramids demonstrate the ingenuity of the ancient Egyptians.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ingenuitās에서 왔고 genius(타고난 재능)와 가까운 말입니다.

senses.en: characterized by an inability to mask your feelings; not devious

examples.text: The child's ingenuous admission that he had eaten the cake made the whole room laugh.

senses.en: Naive and trusting.

examples.text: Only an ingenuous investor would trust a stranger who promised guaranteed returns of fifty percent.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ingenuus '고귀한 성품의, 솔직한'에서 왔습니다. 타고난 그대로 꾸밈이 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: (used especially of ideas or principles) deeply rooted; firmly fixed or held

examples.text: Habits of obedience were so ingrained in the soldiers that they hesitated even when the order was clearly mistaken.

origin.ko: ingrain(깊이 스며들게 하다)에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다. 깊이 배어 뿌리 박힌 상태를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: a person who shows no gratitude

examples.text: After all the help he had received, he proved an ingrate who never once thanked his benefactors.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ingrātus '달갑지 않은'에서 왔습니다. 고마움(grat)을 모르는 사람이라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: gain favor with somebody by deliberate efforts

examples.text: The new intern tried to ingratiate himself with the director by praising every idea she proposed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 in grātiam '~의 호의를 얻으려고'에서 왔습니다. 남의 호감 속으로 파고든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: existing as an essential constituent or characteristic

examples.text: Some risk is inherent in any investment, however carefully the portfolio is diversified.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inhaerēre '~에 딱 붙어 있다'에서 왔습니다. 안에 붙어 떨어지지 않으니 '본질적인'입니다.

senses.en: limit, block, or decrease the action or function of

examples.text: inhibit the action of the enzyme

senses.en: make (someone) self-conscious and as a result unable to act naturally

examples.text: Having the teacher watch from the back of the room inhibited the shy students from speaking.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inhibēre '붙들어 두다, 억제하다'에서 왔습니다. 안에 붙잡아 움직이지 못하게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Harmful in effect.

examples.text: Policies inimical to small businesses drove many shopkeepers out of the city center.

senses.en: not friendly

examples.text: The rival delegation adopted an inimical tone from the first day of the talks.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 inimīcālis '적대적인'에서 왔습니다. 친구(amicus)가 아닌 적이라는 데서 '해로운'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: defying imitation; matchless

examples.text: an inimitable style

origin.ko: 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 inimitabilis에서 왔습니다. 흉내 낼 수 없으니 '독보적인'입니다.

senses.en: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin

examples.text: iniquitous deeds

senses.en: Grossly unfair or unjust.

examples.text: Critics condemned the iniquitous tax, which fell hardest on the poorest families in the district.

origin.ko: iniquity에 -ous가 붙은 말입니다. 공평하지 않음(inīquus)이 사악함의 뜻으로 번졌습니다.

senses.en: morally objectionable behavior

examples.text: The preacher warned that the iniquity of the city's rulers would eventually bring about its downfall.

senses.en: an unjust act

examples.text: The seizure of the farmers' land without payment was widely denounced as an iniquity.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inīquitās '불평등, 불공정'에서 왔습니다. 고르지 않고 공정하지 못한 것이 '부도덕'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a slight suggestion or vague understanding

examples.text: he had no inkling what was about to happen

origin.ko: 중세 영어에서 '암시, 귀띔'을 뜻하던 말에서 왔다고 하며, 정확한 경로는 불확실합니다.

senses.en: not established by conditioning or learning

examples.text: Linguists debate whether humans possess an innate capacity for grammar or acquire it purely through experience.

origin.ko: 라틴어 innātus '타고난'에서 왔습니다. 안에 지닌 채 태어났다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: not injurious to physical or mental health

examples.text: The mushrooms looked innocuous, but several of them were in fact mildly poisonous.

senses.en: not causing disapproval

examples.text: it was an innocuous remark

origin.ko: 라틴어 innocuus '해가 없는'에서 왔습니다. 해치지(noc) 않으니 무해합니다.

senses.en: beyond normal limits

examples.text: The project consumed an inordinate amount of time and money without producing any usable results.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inōrdinātus '정리되지 않은, 무질서한'에서 왔습니다. 질서의 한계를 벗어나 '지나친'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: an inquiry into the cause of an unexpected death

examples.text: The coroner opened an inquest to determine how the hiker had died on the remote mountain trail.

senses.en: An inquiry, typically into an undesired outcome

examples.text: After the humiliating defeat, the party held a bitter inquest into what had gone wrong.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 enqueste에서 왔고 라틴어 '묻다, 조사하다'와 이어집니다. 안을 파고들어 조사한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: showing curiosity

examples.text: The inquisitive child took apart the old radio to see how it worked.

senses.en: Too curious; overly interested; nosy.

examples.text: Her inquisitive neighbors asked endless questions about who visited the house and why.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inquirere '묻다, 조사하다'에서 왔습니다. 안을 파고들어 캐묻는 성격입니다.

senses.en: Difficult or impossible to comprehend, fathom, or interpret.

examples.text: The judge's inscrutable expression gave no hint of how she would rule on the motion.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 īnscrūtābilis '살펴볼 수 없는'에서 왔습니다. 샅샅이 조사해도 알 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: without compunction or human feeling

examples.text: The insensate tyrant ordered the village burned without a second thought for the families inside.

senses.en: devoid of feeling and consciousness and animation

examples.text: The sculptor spoke to the insensate stone as though it could answer her.

senses.en: Senseless; foolish; irrational; thoughtless.

examples.text: The mob's insensate fury destroyed the very market that fed the town.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsēnsātus에서 왔습니다. 느낌(sens)이 없으니 '무감각한'입니다.

senses.en: unaware of or indifferent to

examples.text: The CEO seemed insensible to the growing anger among employees over the sudden layoffs.

senses.en: barely able to be perceived

examples.text: The change in the river's course was so gradual as to be almost insensible.

senses.en: incapable of physical sensation

examples.text: insensible to pain

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 īnsēnsibilis에서 왔습니다. 느낄 수 없는 상태, 곧 의식하지 못함을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: working or spreading in a hidden and usually injurious way

examples.text: glaucoma is an insidious disease

senses.en: Intending to entrap; alluring but harmful.

examples.text: Hansel and Gretel were lured by the witch’s insidious gingerbread house.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsidiae '매복'에서 왔고 insideō '그 위에 앉다'에서 나왔습니다. 숨어서 기다리다 덮친다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: give to understand

examples.text: She insinuated that her friends had betrayed her.

senses.en: introduce or insert (oneself) in a subtle manner

examples.text: He insinuated himself into the conversation of the people at the nearby table

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsinuō '파고들다, 슬며시 들어가다'에서 왔습니다. 굽이진 틈으로 슬쩍 스며들듯 넌지시 비친다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lacking interest or significance or impact

examples.text: The critics dismissed the film as an insipid romance with flat characters and a predictable plot.

senses.en: lacking taste or flavor or tang

examples.text: The diners were disappointed with the plain, insipid soup they were served.

origin.ko: 프랑스어를 거쳐 라틴어 īnsipidus '맛없는'에서 왔습니다. 맛이 없다는 데서 '재미없는'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: be emphatic or resolute and refuse to budge

examples.text: The defendant insisted on his innocence.

senses.en: postulate positively and assertively

examples.text: The author insists that economic growth cannot continue without limits on resource consumption.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsistere '위에 서다, 버티다'에서 왔습니다. 자리를 딛고 물러서지 않는 모습입니다.

senses.en: the trait of being rude and impertinent; inclined to take liberties

examples.text: The captain punished the sailor's insolence by taking away his shore leave for a month.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsolentia에서 왔습니다. 관례(익숙함)에 따르지 않는 건방진 태도입니다.

senses.en: marked by casual disrespect

examples.text: The insolent clerk rolled his eyes and refused to answer the customer's polite question.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsolēns '익숙하지 않은, 오만한'에서 왔습니다. 관례를 따르지 않아 무례해졌습니다.

senses.en: unable to meet or discharge financial obligations

examples.text: an insolvent debtor

origin.ko: in-(아닌)과 solvent(빚을 갚을 수 있는)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 빚을 풀어낼 수 없는 상태입니다.

senses.en: Carelessness, heedlessness, indifference, or casual unconcern.

examples.text: He faced the angry board with an insouciance that only made its members angrier.

origin.ko: 프랑스어에서 왔고 in-(아닌)과 souciant(걱정하는)가 합쳐졌습니다. 걱정이 없는 태연함입니다.

senses.en: supply the inspiration for

examples.text: The article about the artist inspired the exhibition of his recent work

senses.en: serve as the inciting cause of

examples.text: The mayor's evasive answers inspired little confidence among residents worried about the flooded streets.

senses.en: To draw in by the operation of breathing; to inhale.

examples.text: The patient was told to inspire deeply and hold the breath while the scan was taken.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnspīrāre '숨을 불어넣다'에서 왔습니다. 안에 숨(영감)을 불어넣는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: an item of information that is typical of a class or group

examples.text: The company's collapse is a striking instance of what can happen when oversight is neglected.

senses.en: clarify by giving an example of

examples.text: The professor instanced several famine years to show how policy failures magnify natural disasters.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnstantia '가까이 있음, 끈질김'에서 왔습니다. 곁에 서 있는 구체적인 '사례'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: set up or lay the groundwork for

examples.text: The new administration moved quickly to institute reforms in the way public contracts are awarded.

senses.en: an association organized to promote art or science or education

examples.text: I work in a medical research institute.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnstituō '세우다, 설치하다'에서 왔습니다. 어떤 것 위에 기틀을 세운다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: unbearably arrogant or conceited

examples.text: After winning the award he became insufferable, boasting about it to anyone who would listen.

senses.en: too extreme to bear

examples.text: The insufferable heat of the crowded train car left passengers gasping and desperate for the next station.

origin.ko: in-(아닌)과 sufferable(견딜 수 있는)이 합쳐진 말입니다. 참고 견딜 수 없을 정도라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: narrowly restricted in outlook or scope

examples.text: The insular community distrusted outsiders and resisted every attempt to modernize its customs.

senses.en: relating to or characteristic of or situated on an island

examples.text: The insular climate of the archipelago keeps temperatures mild throughout the year.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsulāris '섬의'에서 왔습니다. 섬처럼 고립되어 시야가 좁다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a person who takes part in an armed rebellion against the constituted authority (especially in the hope of improving conditions)

examples.text: Government troops pushed the insurgents out of the northern provinces after months of fighting.

senses.en: Rebellious, opposing authority.

examples.text: The insurgent provinces.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsurgō '~에 맞서 일어나다'에서 왔습니다. 권력에 맞서 일어서는 사람입니다.

senses.en: organized opposition to authority; a conflict in which one faction tries to wrest control from another

examples.text: The army crushed the insurrection within a week, but unrest simmered in the capital for months.

origin.ko: 라틴어 īnsurrēctiō '봉기'에서 왔고 īnsurgō '일어나다'에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: capable of being apprehended or understood

examples.text: Italian and Spanish are partially mutually intelligible languages.

origin.ko: 라틴어 intelligibilis에서 왔습니다. 사이에서 골라 읽어 낼 수 있어 '이해할 수 있는'입니다.

senses.en: have in mind as a purpose

examples.text: He intends to go to university.

senses.en: design or destine

examples.text: The fund was intended to support young researchers, not to cover the institution's running costs.

origin.ko: 라틴어 intendere '~쪽으로 뻗다, 주의를 돌리다'에서 왔습니다. 마음을 한 방향으로 뻗는 것이 '의도하다'입니다.

senses.en: place in a grave or tomb

examples.text: The fallen soldiers were interred with full honors in the cemetery overlooking the valley.

origin.ko: 속라틴어 *interrāre '흙 속에 넣다'에서 왔습니다. 땅속에 묻는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: capable of replacing or changing places with something else; permitting mutual substitution without loss of function or suitability
senses.ko: 교환 가능한, 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있는

examples.text: The two terms are often treated as interchangeable, though careful writers distinguish between them.

origin.ko: inter-(서로)와 change(바꾸다), -able이 합쳐진 말입니다. 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: command against

examples.text: The council moved to interdict the sale of the drug until further safety tests were completed.

senses.en: a court order prohibiting a party from doing a certain activity

examples.text: The court issued an interdict barring the factory from dumping waste into the river.

origin.ko: 라틴어 interdīcō '금지하다'에서 왔습니다. 사이에 끼어들어 말로 막는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a person who takes part in a conversation

examples.text: The diplomat was a patient interlocutor, listening carefully before answering each of the journalist's questions.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 interlocūtor에서 왔습니다. 서로 사이에서 말을 주고받는 사람입니다.

senses.en: tiresomely long; seemingly without end

examples.text: The interminable meeting dragged on for hours while the audience quietly checked their watches.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 interminābilis에서 왔습니다. 끝낼 수 없으니 '끝없는'입니다.

senses.en: stopping and starting at irregular intervals

examples.text: intermittent rain showers

origin.ko: 라틴어 intermittens '중간에 보내는'에서 왔습니다. 사이사이 끊어 내보내니 '간헐적인'입니다.

senses.en: (of conflict) within a group or organization

examples.text: Internecine disputes among the party's factions weakened it far more than any opposition attack.

senses.en: Mutually destructive; most often applied to warfare.

examples.text: The internecine struggle left both armies exhausted and the countryside in ruins.

origin.ko: 라틴어 internecīnus '치명적인'에서 왔고 원래는 '대학살'과 관련됩니다. 영어에서 inter-(사이)로 재해석되어 '내부 갈등'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: reciprocal action and reaction

examples.text: The novel explores the subtle interplay between memory and identity across three generations of one family.

origin.ko: inter-(서로)와 play(작용)가 합쳐진 말입니다. 서로 주고받는 작용을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: insert words into texts, often falsifying it thereby

examples.text: Later copyists interpolated several passages into the manuscript, obscuring the author's original argument.

senses.en: estimate the value of something based on known values

examples.text: Analysts interpolate missing temperature readings from the values recorded at nearby weather stations.

origin.ko: 라틴어 interpolō의 분사 interpolātus에서 왔습니다. 글 사이에 끼워 넣는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the time between two reigns, governments, etc.

examples.text: Several rival nobles competed for power during the long interregnum that followed the king's sudden death.

origin.ko: 라틴어 interrēgnum에서 왔습니다. 두 왕(reign) 사이의 공백기라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: spin, wind, or twist together

examples.text: intertwine the ribbons

senses.en: To become mutually involved.

examples.text: The economies of the two nations have become so intertwined that a crisis in one affects the other.

origin.ko: inter-(서로)와 twine(꼬다)이 합쳐진 말입니다. 서로 꼬여 얽히는 모습입니다.

senses.en: marked by close acquaintance, association, or familiarity

examples.text: an intimate friend

senses.en: concerning things deeply private and personal

examples.text: The memoir reveals intimate details of the author's struggle with illness and her fear of failure.

origin.ko: 라틴어 intimus '가장 안쪽의'에서 왔습니다. 가장 안쪽까지 들어올 만큼 가까운 사이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: an indirect suggestion

examples.text: The minister gave no intimation that a resignation was being considered until the announcement itself.

origin.ko: 라틴어 intimatio에서 왔고 intimate(안으로 넣다)와 이어집니다. 속뜻을 슬쩍 알려 주는 '암시'입니다.

senses.en: not tractable; difficult to manage or mold

examples.text: The intractable mule refused to move, no matter how hard the farmer pulled on the rope.

senses.en: Difficult to deal with, solve, or manage. (of a problem)

examples.text: Decades of negotiation failed to resolve the intractable conflict over the disputed border region.

origin.ko: in-(아닌)과 tractable(끌어 다룰 수 있는)이 합쳐졌습니다. 끌어당겨 다룰 수 없을 만큼 고집이 셉니다.

senses.en: impervious to pleas, persuasion, requests, reason

examples.text: The intransigent union leader rejected every compromise, and the strike entered its third month.

origin.ko: 스페인어를 거쳐 라틴어 trānsigō '합의를 보다'에서 왔습니다. 합의에 이르지 않으려는 완강함입니다.

senses.en: invulnerable to fear or intimidation

examples.text: The intrepid explorers crossed the frozen plateau with little more than sled dogs and a few supplies.

origin.ko: 라틴어 intrepidus에서 왔습니다. 불안해 떠는(trepidus) 일이 없으니 '두려움을 모르는'입니다.

senses.en: cause to be interested or curious

examples.text: The strange symbols carved on the wall intrigued the archaeologists, who spent weeks trying to decipher them.

senses.en: a crafty and involved plot to achieve your (usually sinister) ends

examples.text: The novel follows a web of political intrigue at the royal court, where every courtier plots against a rival.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어를 거쳐 라틴어 intrīcō '얽히게 하다'에서 왔습니다. 얽힌 음모에서 호기심을 끄는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: belonging to a thing by its very nature

examples.text: the intrinsic value of gold or silver

origin.ko: 라틴어 intrīnsecus '안쪽에서'에서 왔습니다. 안에 속해 있으니 '본질적인'입니다.

senses.en: fill quickly beyond capacity; as with a liquid

examples.text: The agency was inundated with phone calls.

senses.en: fill or cover completely, usually with water

examples.text: Heavy rains inundated the valley, forcing hundreds of families to leave their homes overnight.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inundō '범람하다'에서 왔고 unda(물결)에서 나왔습니다. 물결이 밀려드는 모습입니다.

senses.en: cause to accept or become hardened to; habituate

examples.text: Years of covering war zones had inured the reporter to scenes that would horrify most people.

origin.ko: 중세 영어에서 in-과 ure(실행하다, 단련하다)가 합쳐졌습니다. 몸에 배도록 단련시킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Accustomed to something, especially something unpleasant.

examples.text: By now she is inured to their inanities.

origin.ko: inure에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다. 단련되어 몸에 밴 상태입니다.

senses.en: gradually intrusive without right or permission

examples.text: Many users objected to the app's invasive tracking of their location even when it was closed.

senses.en: marked by a tendency to spread especially into healthy tissue

examples.text: invasive cancer cells

origin.ko: 라틴어 invādō '안으로 들어가다, 침입하다'에서 왔습니다. 허락 없이 안으로 밀고 들어오는 느낌입니다.

senses.en: abusive or venomous language used to express blame or censure or bitter deep-seated ill will

examples.text: The debate degenerated into personal invective, with each candidate hurling insults at the other.

origin.ko: 라틴어 invehō '쏟아붓다'에서 온 invectīvus에서 왔습니다. 욕설을 상대에게 퍼붓는다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: influence or urge by gentle urging, caressing, or flattering

examples.text: The salesman tried to inveigle the couple into buying a warranty they clearly did not need.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 '눈이 없는'에서 왔습니다. 눈을 멀게 해 속이고 꾄다는 데서 '감언으로 꾀다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: the ceremonial act of clothing someone in the insignia of an office; the formal promotion of a person to an office or rank

examples.text: The investiture of the new archbishop drew thousands of worshippers to the cathedral.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 investīre '옷을 입히다'에서 왔습니다. 관직의 예복을 입혀 주는 의식입니다.

senses.en: Having had a habit (usually a bad habit) for a long time.

examples.text: An inveterate gambler, he lost his savings again and again despite repeated promises to stop.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inveterātus '오래된, 만성이 된'에서 왔습니다. 오래 묵어 굳은 습관을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: containing or implying a slight or showing prejudice

examples.text: Critics argued that ranking the schools by income created an invidious comparison between poor and rich districts.

senses.en: Causing ill will, envy, or offense.

examples.text: The manager faced the invidious task of choosing which of two equally loyal employees to dismiss.

origin.ko: 라틴어 invidia '질투'에서 왔습니다. '곁눈질로 보다'에서 '시샘하다'로 뜻이 변했습니다.

senses.en: give life or energy to

examples.text: The cold water invigorated him

origin.ko: 새 라틴어 invigōrō에서 왔고 in-과 vigor(활력)가 합쳐졌습니다. 몸속에 힘을 불어넣는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: not capable of being violated or infringed

examples.text: The constitution declares freedom of conscience an inviolable right that no government may override.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inviolābilis '건드릴 수 없는'에서 왔습니다. 범할 수 없으니 '불가침의'입니다.

senses.en: Not violated; free from violation or hurt of any kind; secure against violation or impairment.

examples.text: The remote valley remained inviolate, untouched by roads, mines, or the settlers who had spread elsewhere.

origin.ko: 라틴어 inviolātus에서 왔습니다. 침범당하지 않아 온전한 상태입니다.

senses.en: The act or form of calling for the assistance or presence of some superior being, especially prayer offered to a divine being.

examples.text: The ceremony opened with an invocation asking for guidance and blessing on the gathering.

senses.en: An act of invoking or claiming a legal right.

examples.text: The senator's invocation of executive privilege delayed the inquiry for several months.

origin.ko: 라틴어 invocātiō에서 왔고 invoke(부르다)에서 나왔습니다. 신을 불러 도움을 청하는 기도입니다.

senses.en: cite as an authority; resort to

examples.text: He invoked the law that would save him

senses.en: summon into action or bring into existence, often as if by magic

examples.text: The candidate invoked the memory of past recessions to frighten voters away from her opponent.

senses.en: request earnestly (something from somebody); ask for aid or protection

examples.text: The villagers invoked the gods for rain after a third summer of failed crops.

origin.ko: 라틴어 invocāre '불러서 청하다'에서 왔습니다. 권위나 법을 불러내 근거로 삼는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: highly complex or intricate and occasionally devious

examples.text: He related an involved story about every ancestor since 1895.

senses.en: connected by participation or association or use

examples.text: Several senior officials were found to have been involved in the scheme from its earliest stages.

origin.ko: involve에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다. 안으로 돌돌 말려 얽힌 모습에서 '복잡한'이 되었습니다.
